summary: It's a two-phase roll-and-write: draft dice to use as workers placing them on a shared action board, then solve a polyomino puzzle fitting attractions and dinosaur pens onto your park sheet while connecting everything with paths to the exit. It carries over real thematic weight from the parent game and rewards planning ahead more than most roll-and-writes do.
praised: Successfully translates the worker-placement/park-building feel of Dinosaur Island into a lighter roll-and-write format
Interesting dice-drafting layer adds a strategic wrinkle most roll-and-writes lack
criticised: Fiddly with several systems to track (dice values, DNA, attractions, paths) for a roll-and-write
Some randomness in which dice/actions are available can swing outcomes
Less thematic punch than the full board game it's based on
Rulebook/setup can feel like a lot for a 'write' game

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting tension over shared dice/actions

scoring.why: points come from multiple simultaneous tracks: dinosaur pens, attractions, path connections to exits, and set bonuses, so efficient polyomino packing across categories decides the winner
